title: Exact Tradeoff Between Quantum Error Correction and Quantum Darwinism: An Information-Theoretic No-Go Theorem
authors: Arghya Maity, Kelvin Onggadinata, Teck Seng Koh
abstract: Quantum error correction (QEC) and Quantum Darwinism describe opposing consequences of system-environment interactions: QEC seeks to preserve logical quantum information, whereas Quantum Darwinism explains the emergence of objective classical information through its proliferation into the environment. Despite their common physical origin, no direct quantitative connection between these paradigms has previously been established. We introduce an exactly solvable block-environment model based on the logical GHZ block of the Shor [[9,1,3]] quantum error-correcting code, collectively coupled to N environment qubits. The logical fidelity, Holevo information, and Darwinistic redundancy are obtained systematically for arbitrary environment size and imperfect recovery efficiency. Eliminating the common decoherence parameter yields an exact tradeoff relating Darwinistic redundancy directly to the post-recovery logical fidelity, demonstrating that the emergence of redundant classical records occurs at the expense of logical quantum information. We further prove a model-independent no-go theorem showing that the logical fidelity exceeds a critical threshold precludes the emergence of Darwinistic redundancy, irrespective of the microscopic Hamiltonian or environment structure. The solvable model saturates this general bound, establishing the first quantitative information-theoretic connection between logical quantum information protection and the emergence of redundant classical records.
summary: This paper establishes an exact information-theoretic tradeoff theorem demonstrating that the emergence of redundant classical records via Quantum Darwinism directly degrades the logical fidelity protected by Quantum Error Correction. By analyzing a solvable model, the authors derive a quantitative relationship linking these two seemingly disparate phenomena and prove a general no-go bound governing this competition.
main_problem: The paper establishes a quantitative, information-theoretic tradeoff between Quantum Error Correction (QEC), which preserves quantum coherence, and Quantum Darwinism (QD), which describes the emergence of objective classical information via environmental redundancy.
main_result: An exact, parameter-independent tradeoff theorem is derived showing that increasing redundant classical records (Darwinistic Redundancy) must come at the direct expense of the logical fidelity of the quantum state. Furthermore, a model-independent no-go theorem proves this fundamental limit.
method: The authors analyze an exactly solvable block-environment model by deriving relationships between three key observables: logical fidelity ($F_L$), Holevo information ($\chi$), and decoherence factors ($\Gamma$).
model_or_system: The system uses the logical GHZ block of the Shor code interacting with $N$ environment qubits. The dynamics are analyzed using a Hamiltonian structure, focusing on the resulting decoherence factor $\Gamma_N(t)$ that governs both quantum information loss and environmental entanglement.
key_observables: Logical Fidelity ($F_L^{(N)}$), Holevo Information ($\chi_m$), Darwinistic Redundancy ($R_\delta$), Decoherence Factor ($\Gamma_N(t)$), and Von Neumann Entropy ($S(ho_b)$).
important_parameters: Environment size ($N$), imperfect recovery efficiency ($\eta$), decoherence parameter ($gZ_t$), and the redundancy threshold ($\delta$).
main_assumptions: The initial analytical derivation relies on an exactly solvable limit (e.g., setting one coupling constant to zero), although numerical tests confirm robustness using the full Hamiltonian.
figures_summary: Figures numerically demonstrate the competition between QEC and QD, showing data collapse onto the derived tradeoff equation, confirming critical scaling near thresholds, and verifying the model-independent no-go theorem by plotting $\chi$ vs $F_L$.
paper_structure: The paper systematically introduces the conflict between QEC and QD, develops the solvable block-environment model using the Shor code, derives expressions for fidelity and redundancy based on a common decoherence factor ($\Gamma$), and finally eliminates this factor to establish the exact tradeoff theorem and the general no-go bound.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous, quantitative link between two major concepts in quantum information theory (QEC and QD), suggesting that environmental interaction cannot simultaneously maximize both coherence protection and classical redundancy. This has implications for understanding decoherence mechanisms in realistic physical systems.
